title: Waveform peaks: one unbounded thread + ffmpeg per clip, each buffering the whole decoded clip in the dashboard process
what: With no fleet set in the dashboard mount, peaks_state starts a thread per distinct clip with no cap; each decodes the whole clip to s16le via communicate() and widens it to int32. Failures are not recorded, so the page's ~10 retries over 120 s each re-decode.
cost: Measured per clip: 64 min ~307 MB transient, 120 min ~576 MB. A lane opening on 12 hour-long multicams without .peaks is 4-7 GB at once inside the uvicorn process that serves fleet status; recurs after every re-render.
evidence: probe.py: 61 MB stdout + 246 MB numpy peak (64 min), 115 + 461 MB (120 min); code read; FLEET.md section 12 says the page's peaks path is thread-per-file.
fix: Queue peaks on the existing single lite/src worker and stream the decode in fixed chunks (max-pool per chunk); record failures per (wav, mtime). Keep first-writer-wins, the PK rate header, ETag/304.

title: ProjectAgentEngine runs LibraryEngine.__init__ twice: orphan GoogleTranslator thread + cache per engine, every store read twice
where: MulticamPipeline cards/project_agent.py:115-121; cards/agent.py:66; cards/project_engine.py (ProjectEngine.__init__ -> LibraryEngine.__init__); cards/library_engine.py:419-423, 535-536; cards/translate.py:199-225
what: Diamond construction calls LibraryEngine.__init__ via AgentLink and again via ProjectEngine. The first GoogleTranslator's worker thread is already running and keeps that translator and its parsed cache alive forever with no handle to stop it.
cost: Per engine: +1 thread, +1 in-memory copy of gt_translations.json (estimated a few MB), and double build-time reads of timeline_plans.json (3.4 MB on Civil Defence), notes, place, colours over the vault mount.
evidence: Code read: translate.py:225 starts the worker inside __init__.
ledger: related to PL-RES-77 / bug-dash-jobs-cards-4 (open); this part is new
fix: Make LibraryEngine.__init__ re-entry safe, or stop the first translator before the second init. Keep the write_allow/media_map resets ProjectAgentEngine relies on.

title: A cooperative stop is cheap: ProjectAgentEngine.stop skips LibraryEngine.stop and _lib_worker has no exit
what: Only the library sweep loop and the translator ignore stop; every other worker is flag-aware, drains and exits, or is one-shot. About 10 lines (call LibraryEngine.stop, while not self._stop in _lib_worker, wake it, close the reader) would make engines releasable.
cost: Today each dropped engine leaks per PL-RES-77 (+128 MB, 15 threads); with this fix plus cards-library-2 the pool could evict instead of refuse.
evidence: Code read; LibraryEngine.stop docstring says ProjectAgentEngine.stop does not reach it.
fix: ProjectAgentEngine.stop: set _stop, LibraryEngine.stop(self), _lib_wake.set(), reader.close(); loop on not _stop; drop ring/gz/tokens caches. Pinned jobs still finish.

title: Publish ring keeps 32 full copies of every card dict (~57 MB at 1,522 cards); frames cache duplicates token lists
what: build_state makes fresh card dicts every build, so each of the RING_KEEP=32 entries is a full card set. _frames_cache stores a converted tuple copy of every clip's tokens.
cost: Measured 1.77 MB/version -> 57 MB per engine after 32 bumps on a 1,522-card cut; frames cache +2.0 MB per hour-long interview (about 18 MB for 9). Most of the measured +128 MB per engine.
evidence: probe.py ring; probe2.py frames (2.0 MB vs 0.26 MB as two array('d')).
fix: Keep per-card fingerprints (or last 8 versions) in the ring instead of dicts; store starts/ends as array('d') and index into entry tokens. Keep state_delta patch semantics and first_of_seq.

title: timeline_plans.history.jsonl appends the whole op list per rev: quadratic, never pruned, never read
what: PlanStore._put appends a line with all current ops on every append/undo/mode change.
cost: Measured 70.3 MB for one 400-op insert draft (plans file 340 KB); estimated 10-15 MB for 400 trims/moves; per episode, forever, in the vault and its snapshots.
fix: Append deltas only (full list only when ops shrink) and rotate at a size cap.

title: timeline_place.json rewritten whole, indented, ~1/s per device while the lane plays
what: The moving lane head re-arms a 1 s place save; the server dumps every timeline's record (up to 24 devices, 50 marks, no timeline eviction) each time.
cost: Measured 1.41 MB / 46.7 ms per save at an upper-bound 100 timelines x 24 devices; realistic 50-300 KB estimated; 1 vault write/s per playing device for hours.
evidence: probe.py place section; page code read.
fix: Skip head-only saves during playback (save on pause or every 15 s), compact JSON, evict timelines untouched for 90 days.

title: NoteStore and BinStore unlocked with one fixed .tmp: concurrent saves can raise or corrupt; a corrupt file loads as empty
what: set() on HTTP threads and heal() on the publish/edit thread both json.dump self.data to path+'.tmp' with no lock; RuntimeError is uncaught and two writers can interleave into invalid JSON, which the next load reads as {}.
cost: Rare, but the outcome is every note, stack mark and collapsed state of the episode silently lost.
evidence: Code read; PlanStore/PlaceStore do take a lock.
fix: Lock mutate+snapshot, unique tmp names, set a bad file aside on load instead of overwriting it.

title: Extraction/proxy failures are sticky for the engine's life, even across a root switch
what: _src_fail/_vid_fail record any failure, transient or not, and nothing clears them.
cost: One NAS hiccup or timeout keeps a clip dark on every editor's lane until the dashboard container restarts (weeks).
fix: Store (why, time, src mtime); retry after ~10 min or on mtime change; keep 'no audio track' sticky.

title: Library sweep polls Postgres every 2 s forever, 4 round trips per tick, with or without viewers
what: _lib_worker wakes every 2 s for the container's life; live-on-library it runs a 4-query fingerprint; file mode still wakes and may run _library_default queries every 30 s.
cost: ~2 queries/s = ~173k/day per engine against the project library server, including nights.
fix: One-query fingerprint; back off to 30 s when no api/state was served in 2 min, wake on the next poll.

title: Undo of an in-place library edit is two transactions; failure between them half-restores the timeline; backups never pruned
what: restore() commits the deletion of created rows, then re-inserts and updates in a second transaction; every apply and dry run writes a backup JSON nothing prunes.
cost: A failed second transaction leaves the timeline without the edit's items and without the originals; mitigated by the REAL_LIBRARIES gate (lab libraries only since 2026-09-29).
evidence: Code read; undo's docstring says the restore has already committed.
fix: Do delete + re-insert + update in one transaction on one connection; prune old backups keeping the latest per timeline.

title: remote_audio caches never pruned; crashed encodes leave .tmp files
what: Opus copies, extractions, .peaks and 480p proxies accumulate per clip name forever; renamed clips orphan theirs; a kill mid-encode leaves .tmp* files.
cost: Estimated 0.5-0.7 GB per footage hour for 480p proxies once the video window is used, 20-30 MB/h for audio; unreported.
evidence: Code read; no prune path exists.
fix: At engine start delete *.tmp* older than a day and report remote_audio size on the health line; optional age eviction of unserved proxies.
